title: Compression-aware Probe Suite and Quant Sensitivity Fingerprint
author: Aisha Patel
body:
Summary
-------
This document defines the Compression-aware Probe Suite (CAPS) and the Quant Sensitivity Fingerprint (QSF) used to characterize how model outputs degrade or change under quantized artifacts and compression-friendly runtime transforms. CAPS is intended to be run during model onboarding, pre-rollout checks, and continuous regression scans for Dedicated/Private deployments where quantization and mixed-precision paths are used. QSF is a compact, reproducible vector of metrics that summarizes per-workload sensitivity and drives rollout gating, remediation recommendations, and perf/cost tradeoff UI.

Goals and scope
----------------
- Provide a deterministic, reproducible probe generation and scoring pipeline that surfaces subtle behavioral changes introduced by quantization (post-training quant, dynamic quant, mixed-precision) and compression transforms (activation compression, KV-cache serialization).
- Produce an interpretable fingerprint (QSF) per model+profile+workload that is stable across seeds and informative to engineers and product owners.
- Integrate with the eval harness and CI to: (1) block unsafe rollouts, (2) suggest fallback quant-profiles, and (3) prioritize human review slices.

When to run CAPS
------------------
1. Model onboarding (initial candidate promotion to shadow/dedicated).
2. Before enabling a new quant profile or runtime compression optimization in production.
3. Nightly regression scans focused on quant-related slices.
4. On-demand triage when a production regression correlates with a quant deployment.

High-level components
---------------------
1. Probe generator: produces canonical inputs (prompt families) using mutation operators.
2. Multi-mode runner: executes model variants (fp16/fp32, int8, int8+KV-compress, mixed-precision) through the eval harness with matched seeds and deterministic sampling where applicable.
3. Metric synthesizer: computes per-probe metrics and aggregates into the QSF vector.
4. Triager ruleset: maps QSF deltas to recommended remediation steps and rollout gate outcomes.

Probe generator details
-----------------------
- Prompt families covered (each family contains 500–2000 seeds):
  - Long-context priming: multi-turn histories with varying pivot lengths (1k, 4k, 8k tokens).
  - Short-instruction: terse one-line instructions for copy/transform tasks.
  - Table/structured-output: prompts that request JSON/YAML outputs and strict schema conformance.
  - Retrieval-primed: prompts with embedded retrieved passages that exercise KV cache reuse.
  - Math/precision: numerical reasoning and formula manipulation.
  - Safety probes: adversarial paraphrases and hallucination triggers.
- Mutation operators: token-level dropout, synonym substitution, punctuation perturbation, casing/noise injection, and answer-mask perturbation to probe stability under boundary conditions.
- Sampling strategy: stratified by token-length, by expected generation length, and by instruction complexity score (0–1).

Execution matrix
----------------
- Model variants to compare (example): fp32-reference, fp16, int8-static, int8-dynamic, mixed-precision-layerwise, int8+kv-compress.
- Deterministic seeds where sampling-based metrics are compared; stochastic runs for downstream human-facing diversity checks.
- Runtime modes: streaming vs non-streaming to catch prefix-dependent quant artifacts.

Metrics and how QSF is computed
-------------------------------
CAPS computes the following per-probe metrics; QSF aggregates them into a fixed-length vector (string-labeled metrics). Each metric is averaged using trimmed-mean (10% trim) across seeds.
- EmbeddingDistanceMean: mean cosine distance between reference fp32 embeddings and quantized variant embeddings for the same prompt (embedding model: model@last-layer-average).
- OutputTokenFlipRate: percent of tokens where argmax(token) differs from reference, normalized by token-length.
- LogitDelta90: 90th percentile absolute change in top-5 logits for the first N tokens (N configurable, default 32).
- SchemaIntegrityRate: fraction of structured-output probes that parse to expected JSON schema without correction.
- GenerationDivergenceIndex (GDI): BLEU/ROUGE-style metric adapted for free-form; computed as 1 - normalized semantic similarity (embedding-based) so higher is worse.
- ScalingLatencyImpact: relative change in median latency under workload-aware batching when using quantized kernels (used for perf/cost tradeoffs).
- KVCacheMismatchRate: percent of retrieval-primed probes where the final answer differs when the KV cache path is enabled vs disabled in the quantized runtime.

QSF vector example (ASCII):
[EmbeddingDistanceMean:0.012, OutputTokenFlipRate:0.043, LogitDelta90:0.18, SchemaIntegrityRate:0.92, GDI:0.06, ScalingLatencyImpact:-0.12, KVCacheMismatchRate:0.014]

Interpreting QSF and thresholds
-------------------------------
- Threshold bands (per-metric; example defaults):
  - Green (safe): EmbeddingDistanceMean < 0.02, OutputTokenFlipRate < 0.02, LogitDelta90 < 0.10, SchemaIntegrityRate > 0.97, GDI < 0.03, KVCacheMismatchRate < 0.005.
  - Yellow (caution): EmbeddingDistanceMean 0.02–0.05, OutputTokenFlipRate 0.02–0.05, LogitDelta90 0.10–0.25, SchemaIntegrityRate 0.90–0.97, GDI 0.03–0.10, KVCacheMismatchRate 0.005–0.02.
  - Red (fail): values outside yellow bounds.
- Rollout gating policy (example):
  1. All metrics in Green -> allow rollout.
  2. Any metric in Yellow but no metric in Red -> canary rollout with 5% traffic + manual review of top-3 slices flagged.
  3. Any metric in Red -> block and create incident ticket assigned to "serving-quant-team".

Integration with eval harness and CI
-----------------------------------
- CAPS exports a machine-readable QSF JSON artifact per job and a human-readable PDF summary with the top-10 failed probes and sample transcripts.
- Suggested CI step: compare QSF against baseline QSF artifact using a tolerant comparator that respects metric covariances. Failing jobs should not auto-promote.
- Example CLI invocation (eval harness adapter):
  rwi-eval run --suite CAPS --model model:v3-7 --variants fp32,int8,int8-kv --out qsf.json --seeds 42,43,44 --report pdf

Example QSF YAML snippet used by gating service
----------------------------------------------
| param | value |
|-------|-------|
| gating_policy | quant-cautious |
| allowed_yellow_metrics | ["EmbeddingDistanceMean","ScalingLatencyImpact"] |
| blocked_red_metrics | ["SchemaIntegrityRate","KVCacheMismatchRate"] |

(Implementation note: stored in the rollout service as plain YAML; use the eval-harness comparator library to compute deltas.)

Recommended remediation playbook
--------------------------------
1. If SchemaIntegrityRate drops: revert to earlier quant-profile that preserves structured decoders, or enable output-constrained decoding (beam constraints / format validators).
2. If EmbeddingDistanceMean increases but token flip rate is low: prefer hybrid-embedding-recompute (recompute embedding reference on the quantized path for similarity-based downstreams) and add embedding-stable calibration layer.
3. If KVCacheMismatchRate > threshold: audit KV serialization path and test with different cache serialization precisions; consider disabling aggressive KV compression for affected layers.
4. If Latency improves but GDI increases: surface cost/perf tradeoff to product owner and consider partial rollout with fallback routing for safety-sensitive routes.

Ownership and runbook triggers
-----------------------------
- Primary owner: applied-ml (probe infra) team. Secondary: serving-quant team.
- SLOs for CAPS jobs:
  - CAPS job completion (nightly run): 95% jobs finish within 3 hours per model family.
  - QSF artifact availability: 99% within 10 minutes of job completion.
- Runbook triggers (automated):
  - New QSF with any Red metric -> create P1 ticket to #serving-quant on Slack + PagerDuty paging to oncall in the quant rotation.
  - Canary rollout flagging yellow metrics -> open a canary review task and schedule a 1-hour deep-dive with model owner and serving engineer.

Reporting and dashboards
------------------------
- QSF time-series: track per-model, per-profile QSF metrics and highlight metric drift beyond 3-sigma over a 14-day window.
- Heatmap: compression-sensitivity heatmap by probe family (rows = probe family, cols = quant profile) showing %Delta in GDI.
- Example dashboard panels to create:
  - Top failing probes table (probe id, metric, delta, example transcript).
  - QSF trend line per metric with rolling baseline.
  - Rollout gate status for active canaries.

Annotation and human-in-the-loop review guidance
-----------------------------------------------
- For any canary with Yellow or Red metrics, generate an annotation packet with: 10 representative probes, reference transcripts, quantized transcripts, and an embedding-based divergence explanation.
- Human reviewers should answer: (1) Are the failures semantic or surface-level? (2) Do safety or correctness slices exist? (3) Can a prompt rewrite or output filter mitigate? Record decisions in the review artifact.

Examples and quick-start
------------------------
1) Run baseline CAPS locally (dev):
   - rwi-eval local --suite CAPS --model model:v3-7 --variants fp32,int8 --seeds 100 --out dev-qsf.json
2) Upload results for gating check:
   - rwi-gate check --artifact dev-qsf.json --baseline gs://qsf-baselines/model-v3-7/baseline-qsf.json
3) Produce human report:
   - rwi-report render --artifact dev-qsf.json --format pdf --examples 10 --out ./reports/dev-qsf.pdf

Appendix: sample probe table (excerpt)
-------------------------------------
| probe_id | family | seed_length | mutation | expected_behavior | notes |
| P-0001 | long-context | 4096 | token-dropout-0.02 | stable-entity-tracking | useful for KV stress tests |
| P-0420 | table-output | 128 | schema-mask | strict-json | parse fail modes are prioritized |
| P-1337 | math-precision | 64 | numeric-round | exact-equals | checks arithmetic operator stability |

Implementation checklist for eng teams
-------------------------------------
- [ ] Add CAPS suite to model onboarding pipeline (onboarding CI stage 3).
- [ ] Store QSF artifacts in artifact-store with per-model+profile keys.
- [ ] Integrate eval-harness comparator to the gating service and set default thresholds.
- [ ] Create dashboard panels in Grafana and a periodic digest to model owners.

Glossary
--------
- QSF: Quant Sensitivity Fingerprint.
- CAPS: Compression-aware Probe Suite.
- GDI: Generation Divergence Index.
- KV compression: any runtime transform that reduces KV cache memory footprint (quantized serialization, lossy encoding).

Contact and feedback
--------------------
If you have questions or want this suite extended for multimodal models or private deployment constraints (air-gapped artifact storage, offline-only probes), open a merge request against the CAPS repo and ping @Aisha Patel on Slack.
